item.title: InSARFlow: Riemannian Flow Matching for Interferometric SAR
item.description: arXiv:2611.00003v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) enables the analysis of topological changes in natural sites or urban areas. This technique operates by recovering the surface displacement from the study of the phase difference (interferogram) between two or multiple SAR images of the same scene at different times. In practice, the use of phase denoising algorithms is necessary to extract relevant information from the interferograms, which motivated numerous developments in the past decade. Due to the inherent periodicity of phases, interferograms can naturally be represented as points on a Riemannian manifold (specifically, the flat torus). This strong prior knowledge motivates the design of learning-based methods that respect the interferogram's intrinsic geometric constraints. Building on this observation, this paper introduces InSARFlow: a generative modeling framework for the denoising and generation of interferograms. Unlike conventional deep learning approaches formulated in Euclidean spaces, which may violate phase periodicity and produce invalid estimates, this method leverages Riemannian flow matching to learn distributional transports directly on the torus. The interest of this approach is demonstrated on two use cases: (1) realistic interferogram generation, in which we model the transport between uniform noise on the torus to real-world interferograms; (2) interferogram denoising, where InSARFlow transports noisy interferograms to their denoised counterparts. Extensive experiments on a controlled synthetic dataset validate the effectiveness of InSARFlow for interferogram denoising. The proposed approach consistently outperforms studied baselines, highlighting the benefits of geometry-aware learning on the torus. Code and weights available at https://github.com/lebellig/insarflow.
item.dc:creator: Georges Le Bellier (LIP, OCKHAM, CEDRIC - VERTIGO), Arnaud Breloy (CEDRIC - VERTIGO), Nicolas Audebert (IGN, CEDRIC - VERTIGO, UR-LSTI-ENSMSE)

item.title: Coarse-to-Fine Diffusion with Residual Prior for Low-Dose CT Denoising
item.description: arXiv:2611.00016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low-dose CT (LDCT) reduces radiation exposure but often introduces severe noise and streak artifacts that obscure subtle anatomical structures. Existing diffusion-based denoising methods commonly rely on implicit assumptions about the noise distribution, which may not hold in practical LDCT scenarios and can degrade denoising performance. To address this limitation, we propose a Residual-Guided Diffusion framework that effectively incorporates an explicit difference prior to inform the diffusion process of noise distribution. The difference prior is computed as the residual between the LDCT image and a coarse clean estimate, constraining diffusion sampling to a plausible residual space. We further adopt a coarse-to-fine strategy in which a pre-trained RED-CNN provides the coarse estimate to anchor global anatomy, and the diffusion model refines the remaining details under the prior guidance. For efficiency, we employ accelerated sampling with 20 steps at inference. Experiments on three representative datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in both quantitative and qualitative performance measures.
item.dc:creator: Ping Wu, Pengcheng Zheng, Jiahao Zhang, Bohao Chen, Yazhou Ren, Xiaorong Pu

item.title: Exact Dice Degradation Envelopes for Label-Free Segmentation Update Selection
item.description: arXiv:2611.00021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Test-time segmentation updates can improve an unlabeled input while damaging another. Confidence and transformation consistency can rank candidates, but do not in themselves bound the loss caused by returning a changed mask. We derive the exact largest decrease in binary Dice between a baseline and a candidate, maximized over every possible unknown reference mask on the same pixels. A maximizing reference always lies inside baseline foreground: three observable mask counts reduce the problem to at most four reference-cardinality checks. Accepting an output only when its envelope is below a budget gives a deterministic, per-case Dice degradation limit relative to the baseline. A finite grid of logit interpolations permits partial candidate outputs without extra network forwards. Exhaustive and randomized validation checks 5,026,592 reference masks with no discrepancy. We evaluate six independently trained MK-UNet sources, three seeds per task, on ClinicDB, Massachusetts Buildings and the external Kvasir-SEG cohort, including appearance corruptions. Across 17,808 case-condition-seed evaluations, 0 certificate violations occur in the checked candidate comparisons. At a one-point Dice budget, exact versus loose interpolation changes the returned mask in the following fractions of episodes (ClinicDB: 51.0% versus 38.7%; Buildings: 62.1% versus 53.1%; Kvasir-SEG: 52.3% versus 34.9%). Mean Dice effects and useful-update rejection are reported separately from admissibility. An exploratory oracle-presence-bit ablation examines how weak supervision relaxes the empty-baseline restriction. The envelope quantifies relative mask-change risk; it does not certify anatomical correctness, preserve other metrics, or guarantee adaptation benefit.
item.dc:creator: Yuvraj Verma

item.title: Uncertainty-Aware Airlight-Aligned Dual-Gain Recovery with Exact RGB Feasibility for Training-Free Single-Image Dehazing
item.description: arXiv:2611.00052v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The inverse atmospheric-scattering model amplifies transmission, airlight, and sensor-noise errors when a scalar gain $1/t$ is applied in dense haze. We introduce A$^2$CR, a training-free recovery operator that decomposes the airlight-centered RGB residual into components parallel and perpendicular to the airlight vector. Two gains are obtained from analytic quadratic risks containing transmission, airlight, and noise uncertainty. Each gain pair is constrained by the exact convex polygon induced by the six RGB-cube inequalities and gain bounds. An edge-aware joint total-variation problem is solved with a primal-dual algorithm and exact polygon projection. On a controlled DIODE RGB-D evaluation comprising 500 frames and 22,500 reproducible haze recipes, the full variant improves over scalar inversion by $2.951$ dB PSNR (95% bootstrap CI $[2.900,3.001]$), $0.191$ SSIM $[0.187,0.196]$, and $-0.978$ CIEDE2000 $[-1.074,-0.883]$, while eliminating post-recovery RGB violations. Results on four real paired datasets are mixed and were not blind: the method is strongest on Dense-Haze but does not dominate RFEP, DCP, and Haze-Lines elsewhere. We therefore claim an interpretable constrained recovery study, not state-of-the-art dehazing. Code, 64 executable numerical and regression tests, manifests, and statistical artifacts accompany the paper.
item.dc:creator: Maksim Sitnikov (Independent Researcher)

item.title: Toward Contrast-Free Breast MRI: Improving Cancer Detection With Virtual Contrast Enhanced Imaging
item.description: arXiv:2611.00140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although contrast-enhanced (CE) breast MRI is an important tool for cancer detection, intravenous gadolinium administration introduces additional considerations for patients and clinical workflows. AI based virtual contrast enhanced (VCE) MRI could help identify patients for whom acquired CE imaging may be avoidable without compromising diagnostic performance. We developed a framework that combines non contrast (NC) and VCE MRI predictions for cancer detection. On the held-out test set, cancer detection using NC MRI alone achieved an AUROC of 0.865. Combining the predictions from NC and VCE MRI improved AUROC to 0.901. Building on this complementary predictive value, we evaluated patient-level routing to progressively replace acquired CE examinations with the NC plus VCE pathway, prioritizing patients with the most confident NC predictions. This simulation suggests that diagnostic performance can be largely preserved while limiting acquired CE imaging to approximately 40% of patients. Together, these findings demonstrate the complementary value of VCE MRI and suggest its potential to support selective contrast use in breast cancer screening.
item.dc:creator: Hongxi Chen, Sunwoo Kwak, Sanyukta Adap, Katerina Dodelzon, Paula Feldman, Mert R. Sabuncu

item.title: Interpretable Multiple-Instance Learning of Glomerular Pathomics and Subtype Ratios for eGFR Classification
item.description: arXiv:2611.00151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chronic kidney disease is characterized by structural alterations in renal tissue and progressive loss of kidney function. While glomerular subtype ratios provide a compact and clinically meaningful summary of glomerular composition, representing pathomic information using whole-slide image (WSI)-level mean values diminishes glomerulus-level heterogeneity and the contribution of less prevalent patterns. In this proof-of-concept study, we investigated whether modeling individual glomeruli using multiple-instance learning (MIL) could provide complementary information to conventional subtype ratios for estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) classification. We analyzed 162 kidney-biopsy WSIs from 162 patients, categorizing renal function as eGFR < 60 or >= 60 mL/min/1.73 m^2. Quantitative size, shape, intensity, and texture features were extracted from segmented glomeruli, representing each patient as a bag of glomerular instances. An attention-based MIL model was trained to aggregate these heterogeneous pathomic profiles. We evaluated subtype ratios, pathomics, and their combination using ABMIL, with a mean-pooled multilayer perceptron baseline. In five-fold cross-validation, the subtype-ratio-only model achieved an AUC of 0.7262 +/- 0.0596. MIL using pathomics alone achieved an AUC of 0.7362 +/- 0.0788, whereas integrating pathomics with subtype ratios produced the highest mean AUC of 0.7630 +/- 0.0665. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to examine individual feature contributions. These results demonstrate that MIL-based pathomics can complement established glomerular subtype ratios by capturing additional glomerulus-level information for quantitative kidney-biopsy analysis.
item.dc:creator: Tianyu Shi, Yuechen Yang, Leiyue Zhao, Daniel Reisenb\"uchler, Jing Jin, Thangamani Muthukumar, Kenji Ikemura, Mert R. Sabuncu, Yihe Yang, Ruining Deng

item.title: FlowFPR: Flow Matching Prior for Oversampled Fourier Phase Retrieval
item.description: arXiv:2611.00157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fourier phase retrieval reconstructs images from magnitude measurements without phase information, but noise and channel ambiguities make natural color-image recovery challenging. Although diffusion-prior methods provide strong image constraints, their recovery can deteriorate under stronger measurement noise, and repeated generative updates incur substantial computational cost. This paper proposes FlowFPR, which integrates a pretrained Flow Matching prior with relaxed averaged alternating reflections for oversampled Fourier phase retrieval. Each outer iteration obtains a clean image estimate through a single time-dependent Flow prediction, applies measurement-consistency correction, and reconstructs the next path state after fusing the two candidates. This process requires no backpropagation of measurement errors through the Flow network. To address ineffective or excessive correction caused by prescribed fusion weights and fixed inner depths, we introduce adaptive fusion based on residual improvement and a controlled inner search combining early stopping with best-so-far candidate selection. Their combination yields a joint variant alongside the basic method and the two independent improvements. Experiments on natural face images under a common ground-truth-assisted multiple-restart evaluation protocol show that the joint variant achieves the best mean quality among the evaluated methods at the two tested nonzero noise levels, while same-hardware timing demonstrates lower end-to-end runtime than the diffusion-based baselines.
item.dc:creator: Li Jiatai, Cao Wenfei, Chen Yang

item.title: A Rate-Distortion Optimized Skip Mode Coding Framework for Neural Video Compression in AVS
item.description: arXiv:2611.00181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the development of deep learning, neural video compression (NVC) is gaining increasing interest and is currently under standardization in the AVS (Audio Video Coding Standard). Skip mode coding, a crucial component in the traditional video compression, is also adopted in AVS NVC. Although the skip mode takes a large portion in encoding the motion and residual features in the NVC, there is a lack of investigation on the rate distortion performance of the skip mode coding. In this paper, we first thoroughly investigate the rate and distortion distribution in the skip mode coding within a spatial frame and under different temporal reference qualities, and demonstrate that distortion distribution changes spatially and temporally. Therefore, a rate-distortion optimized skip mode coding (RDOSkip) framework is proposed, where the rate and distortion in the skip mode coding is formulated based on a statistical distribution predicted by the hyperprior and the Bayes' theorem. An adaptive skip mode decision method based on spatial-temporal joint RD optimization is developed for the skip mode coding among channels and frames in a group of pictures. It addresses the limitation of the rigid fixed-distortion distribution assumption in skip mode coding within the existing methods that rely on a fixed skip threshold. The temporal skip mode decision method has been adopted in the ongoing AVS NVC standard and incorporated into the reference software. The proposed RDOSkip can be directly used in the inference without any training and with negligible complexity increase. Experimental results further demonstrate that the proposed RDOSkip can improve the performance by 0.90% and 1.29% on AVS and HEVC datasets, respectively, in terms of BD-rate saving.
item.dc:creator: Yuntian Jiang, Shuai Li, Yanbo Gao, Jinglin Zhang, Hui Yuan, Mao Ye

item.title: Does Vendor Image Processing Matter? Learning Echocardiography Display Appearance from Native Beamspace Data
item.description: arXiv:2611.00184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most echocardiography datasets contain vendor-processed images, but processing is often undocumented and may affect model performance and robustness. To address this, we train a small convolutional neural network to reproduce General Electric display appearance from native beamspace brightness-mode ultrasound, using 8 406 recordings from 605 unique patients. The beamspace CNN reduces test mean absolute error by 43% over the optimal pointwise brightness map, outperforms an equivalent Cartesian CNN and runs in real time on a CPU. Across the EchoXFlow and CAMUS datasets, unfiltered training followed by filtered evaluation yields the lowest mean Dice for every class, suggesting filtering may be useful as augmentation when evaluation data are filtered or their processing is unknown. Code and pretrained weights: https://github.com/Ahus-AIM/EchoAppearance
item.dc:creator: Elias Stenhede, Arian Ranjbar

item.title: VC-1K: A Diverse Video Test Set for Real-Time Communication
item.description: arXiv:2611.00192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Video Conferencing 1000 (VC-1K), an open-source test set comprising approximately 1,000 video sequences specifically designed for evaluating video processing and encoding pipelines in real-time communication (RTC) scenarios. Unlike existing test sets that primarily rely on studio-produced or screen content, VC-1K consists of user-generated video call content captured on consumer mobile devices under a wide variety of conditions. The dataset predominantly features talking-head sequences with distinct faces, but also includes a small subset of outward-facing, rear-camera videos without faces to reflect additional common RTC use cases. It spans a wide range of real-world variables including device type, lighting conditions, motion levels, indoor/outdoor environments, and demographic diversity. All video sequences are accompanied by synchronous audio to facilitate multimodal research. We detail the dataset's design methodology and statistical distribution, and demonstrate its utility through a comparative encoder evaluation of OpenH264, SVT-AV1, and libaom under constant bitrate (CBR) encoding at resolutions typical of RTC deployments. Furthermore, two super-resolution approaches, RealESRGAN and GFPGAN, are evaluated on VC-1K, highlighting the dataset as a useful benchmark for pre- and post-processing research. VC-1K is intended to serve as a publicly available dataset for the video RTC research community.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Chen Sun, Jie Dong, Sergey Sablin, Hassene Tmar, Sriram Srinivasan

item.title: Directional Dual-Head Supervision for Real-Time Source-Free Polyp Segmentation
item.description: arXiv:2611.00238v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) is critical for medical image segmentation as it adapts a model to an unlabeled target domain without accessing source data, thereby preserving data privacy. However, its effectiveness is often limited by confirmation bias: self-training models tend to miss small polyps, hallucinate foreground, and produce imprecise contours. We propose MedRT-SFSeg, a real-time SFDA framework built on a dual-head one-to-one/one-to-many YOLO segmentation architecture. Mask-DHF fuses precision- and recall-oriented predictions into stable pseudo-instances, while DURR uses the sign of pixel-level dual-head disagreement as a directional cue to expand or shrink masks, and additionally recovers missed instances and suppresses hallucinations. Seg-MARD further regularizes feature representations through mask-guided, region-stratified sampling. Experiments on bidirectional adaptation between Kvasir-SEG and CVC-ClinicDB show that MedRT-SFSeg achieves 80.43%/80.77% Dice and 5.53/8.44 mm ASD, improving the non-adapted baseline by 7.7 and 9.8 Dice points while running at more than 62 FPS end-to-end. These results suggest that segmentation-aware dual-head supervision can improve pseudo-label quality without sacrificing real-time inference. Project page: https://danielnguyen-05.github.io/MedRT-SFSeg
item.dc:creator: Hai-Dang Nguyen, Nhat-Khoi Le, Huu-Thuan Huynh, Minh-Triet Tran, Trung-Nghia Le

item.title: The MASSIMAL Dataset: UAV Hyperspectral Images and Ground Truth Observations for Coastal Habitat Mapping in Norway
item.description: arXiv:2611.00763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The MASSIMAL dataset was collected in an effort to develop new remote sensing methods for mapping shallow water coastal habitats, such as kelp forests, seagrass meadows and maerl beds. The main component of the dataset is a set of hyperspectral images collected using a unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). Images were collected during 45 UAV flights performed at 4 main areas along the Norwegian coast, spanning across a wide latitude range, from 59 to 67 degrees north. The ground sampling distance of the hyperspectral images is 3.5 cm, and the spectral range is 400-1000 nm, sampled across 300 spectral bands. During acquisition, push-broom imagery was automatically split into images with a maximum along-track length of 2000 lines. Out of approximately 1000 hyperspectral images, 221 have been annotated, using segmentation masks and a hierarchical taxonomy. An open source image processing pipeline has been developed as part of the dataset preparation, enabling efficient generation of reflectance images and glint-corrected images based on published radiance images. The dataset also includes color images (RGB) and multispectral images collected using UAV, and georeferenced image mosaics constructed from these. Ground truth data supporting the remote sensing images include hours of underwater video, thousands of geotagged underwater images, and tens of kilometers of single-beam sonar data. The data provide a foundation for assessing habitat distribution, tracking changes, and evaluating ecosystem services, thus supporting evidence-based management in Norwegian coastal environments.
item.dc:creator: Martin Hansen Skjelvareid, Eli Rinde, Kasper Hancke, Katalin Blix, Galice Guillaume Hoarau, Nicolo Grometto, Maia R{\o}st Kile

item.title: Adaptive Land Units from Earth Embeddings
item.description: arXiv:2611.01050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modeling land use starts with a choice of spatial units, typically a regular grid of pixels whose resolution is set by the spatial detail the process requires and, often more critically, by the computational budget. With Earth observation data more abundant than ever, we ask whether good land units can instead emerge from the data itself. To do that, we cluster AlphaEarth embeddings with a parallel Bayesian hierarchical clustering into adaptive land units, large where the land is uniform and small where it is highly heterogeneous. Using Denmark as a case study, we turn 402M land pixels into 1.27M newly defined units, about 320 times fewer, without any labels (i.e., unsupervised), making it possible to fit the whole country on a single consumer-grade GPU. Importantly, these units describe the land well, as a regular grid needs about 5 times as many cells to match them against land-use labels, and about 4 times as many against the declared crop of every field. Compared to clustering the satellite images themselves, the embeddings need half the units for the same purity. But more notably, they work as modeling units. Land-use maps learned on them are within a few points of accuracy of pixel models at a small fraction of the cost, and they make whole-country land-use estimates with reliable uncertainty possible in under a minute, where the same model on pixels does not even fit in device memory.
item.dc:creator: Albert Alonso, Jamal Jokar Arsanjani, Andres R. Masegosa

item.title: OpenULF: A Modular Toolkit Enables Data-Driven Ultra-Low-Field MRI with both Classical and Quantum Sensors
item.description: arXiv:2611.01511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultra-low-field (ULF) Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) offers a portable, low-cost alternative to conventional scanners by operating at field strengths below 10 mT. At these fields, two sensor technologies compete: quantum SQUID (Superconducting Quantum Interference Device) sensors, which provide high sensitivity but require cryogenic cooling, and classical induction coils, which are inexpensive and room-temperature but produce weaker signals. With conventional physics-based imaging, both suffer from low signal-to-noise ratios (SNR). Data-driven reconstruction has overcome similar limits in related inverse problems, but its use for ULF-MRI has been hindered by a lack of open datasets, benchmarks, and flexible simulators. To close this gap, we present OpenULF, a modular, open-source simulation toolkit that generates paired training data and supports end-to-end machine-learning (ML) reconstruction. OpenULF integrates a Bloch-equation-validated physics simulator, calibrated SQUID and coil receiver models, reconstruction ML networks, and an automated design-space exploration engine. Architecturally, a receiver abstract base class, a typed HDF5 contract that decouples physics from learning, and a resumable sweep engine make sensors, models, and datasets independently substitutable. Using OpenULF, we train 774 models across four anatomical datasets and conduct three design-space explorations. The effectiveness of ML reconstruction depends strongly on the dataset and the sensor. We identify a SQUID-to-coil crossover near 450 $\mu$T and demonstrate that sensor hardware and ML model capacity can be traded off during system design. Sensor and reconstruction choices must therefore be co-designed: the best sensor is set by the dataset and field strength, not by SNR.
item.dc:creator: Hanhan Wu, Yuchen Yuan, Weiwen Jiang

item.title: Task-driven sparse-view planar X-ray computed tomography for axial metrology
item.description: arXiv:2611.01537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computational imaging can reduce the acquisition burden when the system is designed around task-relevant information rather than complete image recovery. We investigate this framework for sparse-view planar X-ray tomography (XCT) of layered objects, using measurement of the axial termination gap (ATG) of back-drilled printed-circuit-board (PCB) vias as a representative task. Instead of using 3D reconstruction, the proposed method estimates ATG directly from polychromatic projection data through a physics-based sensitivity model. A gated hierarchical estimator first fits ATG together with radiometric perturbations and selectively introduces global geometry and specimen-warp models only when a reduced chi-squared adequacy test and Bayesian information criterion justify the added degrees of freedom. The same low-dimensional perturbation model is incorporated into marginalized Fisher-information analyses, yielding task-specific conditional and calibration-aware Cram'er-Rao bounds. Numerical experiments show that, under a fixed total photon budget, task-driven metrology changes little over 12-64 views, while reconstruction-driven metrology is strongly view-dependent with much larger errors. The direct estimator also follows the expected photon-limited scaling. These results demonstrate a computational sensing strategy in which XCT acquisition, physical modeling, and inference are evaluated according to the quantitative information required by the task rather than for general-purpose volumetric image fidelity.
item.dc:creator: Yibin Tian, Shuming Yang, Wolfgang Heidrich

item.title: Cross-Dataset Generalization of Glaucoma Detection CNNs: Effects of Operating Threshold, Multi-Source Training, and Color Normalization
item.description: arXiv:2611.01992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep learning models for glaucoma detection are usually tested on images from the same dataset used for training. That says little about how they will work at a new hospital or with a new camera. We fine-tuned five ImageNet-pretrained CNNs (ResNet50, DenseNet121, MobileNetV2, EfficientNet-B0, InceptionV3) with identical settings on one of three public fundus datasets (ACRIMA, ORIGA, RIM-ONE DL). Each was tested on a held-out part of its own dataset and on the other two datasets in full. We used three random seeds and report mean and SD over seeds. Mean in-domain AUC was 0.913 and cross-source AUC was 0.702, a drop of 0.211 (SD 0.030; 95% CI 0.135 to 0.286). After correction for multiple comparisons we found no evidence that any architecture did better, though three seeds give low power. At thresholds set on the source validation data, specificity fell from 0.870 to 0.506 and sensitivity from 0.831 to 0.726. Resetting the threshold on 10% of the target images raised specificity to 0.670 but lowered sensitivity to 0.609, and balanced accuracy rose only from 0.616 to 0.639. Training on two sources together did not help (held-out AUC 0.695 versus 0.702). LAB reference normalization (cross-source AUC 0.755) and strong color augmentation (0.754) gave similar gains, cutting the drop to about 0.16. Ben Graham normalization (0.733) and CLAHE (0.712) helped less, and gray-world (0.696) did not help. The two best methods raised specificity but lowered sensitivity. On G1020, used only for testing, AUC stayed near 0.5 in every condition, and networks trained within G1020 were also close to chance. Strong in-domain results do not show that a glaucoma model will work on new data. Normalization and color augmentation reduce the drop but do not remove it. Studies should report external validation and check the operating threshold, not only AUC.
item.dc:creator: Al-Amin Rahman, Saifuddin Ahmed, Resalat Ahmed

item.title: Resampling-based batch reweighting for ComBat harmonization of MRI radiomic features in a multi-scanner glioma cohort
item.description: arXiv:2611.02156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Radiomic features derived from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are sensitive to scanners; therefore, they require harmonization across scanners. In a radiomic feature dataset, some batches may be severely underrepresented compared to the others e.g., the Erasmus Glioma Database, which may provide harmonized features biased towards the larger batches in the dataset. We investigated whether reweighting underrepresented scanner batches before empirical-Bayes ComBat estimation improves feature harmonization and reduces residual scanner association while retaining grade-related information. In this retrospective, the Erasmus Glioma Database included 733 eligible patients acquired at a single center across nine vendor-by-field-strength configurations. Structural MRI acquired at 1 T, 1.5 T, and 3 T; four structural MRI sequences were analyzed. From four structural MRI sequences, 428 features were computed using an IBSI-compliant PyRadiomics implementation. The sample sizes of some scanner batches were very small compared to others, which may produce unequal precision and shrinkage of batch-effect estimates. We proposed a data augmentation approach to overcome the limitation of ComBat. We provided exploratory evidence, along with confirmatory Kruskal-Wallis tests with a Benjamini-Hochberg correction to assess the proposed method. Before harmonization, 392/428 features (91.6%) differed significantly across scanner batches (median eta-squared=0.463). Standard ComBat reduced this to 13/428 (3.0%), whereas batch-augmented ComBat reduced it to 8/428 (1.9%); the median residual effect size was <0.001 for both harmonized conditions. Batch augmentation appeared to be a useful strategy to improve the performance of ComBat for feature harmonization under severe batch-size imbalance.
item.dc:creator: Rifa Sajda Tasnim, Yushuf Sharke, Md Forhad Hossain, Rakibur Rahman, Enamul Hoque Bhuiyan

item.title: Spectral-spatial vision test-time training for hyperspectral image classification
item.description: arXiv:2611.02364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification requires the representation of contiguous spectral signatures and spatial context under limited labeled supervision. Vision test-time training (TTT) offers an alternative to fixed-weight token mixing by performing self-supervised inner-model updates on the input sequence, but its application to center-pixel HSI classification remains insufficiently characterized. We present ViTTT-HSI, a spectral-spatial adaptation of the vision test-time training (ViT3) architecture. A spectral-aware embedding stem extracts ordered-band information using spectral convolution and forms spatial tokens without reducing their spatial resolution. Two ViT3-based TTT encoder blocks perform patch-conditioned token mixing, followed by the fusion of center-pixel and neighborhood-average features for classification. We evaluate the framework on Indian Pines, Pavia University, Salinas, and Houston 2013 using ten random seeds and dataset-specific training fractions of 1% or 5%. The mean overall accuracies are 97.6390%, 98.8753%, 99.3292%, and 98.4283%, respectively. Ablations reveal a substantial contribution from the TTT inner update on Indian Pines and a smaller positive contribution on Pavia University, while the relative benefits of the spectral stem and feature fusion depend on the dataset. The results demonstrate the feasibility of using patch-conditioned vision TTT for spectral--spatial HSI classification and highlight the role of the inner adaptation mechanism.
item.dc:creator: Xiang Zhao

item.title: Shared-Pattern Collaborative Network for Multi-Source Remote Sensing Data Classification
item.description: arXiv:2611.03069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-source remote sensing data classification has received growing attention recently. However, existing methods still struggle to jointly model long-range contextual dependencies and shared spatial patterns across heterogeneous modalities. To address this issue, we propose a Shared-Pattern Collaborative Network (SPCNet) for HSI and SAR/LiDAR joint classification. To enhance cross-modal collaborative learning, Shared-Pattern Collaborative Block (SPCB) is designed by introducing a shared large-kernel operator and a dynamic convolution branch, enabling the network to capture common spatial structures and content-adaptive local features. Furthermore, Region-Adaptive Modality Allocator (RAMA) is developed to assign spatially varying modality weights for reliable feature fusion. Experiments on Houston2013, Augsburg, and Houston2018 datasets demonstrate that SPCNet achieves superior classification performance over several state-of-the-art methods. The code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/oucailab/SPCNet
item.dc:creator: Chenfang Yang, Chuanzheng Gong, Feng Gao, Junyu Dong, Qian Du

item.title: Cross-Layer Refinement and Frequency-aware Fusion Network for Multi-Source Remote Sensing Image Classification
item.description: arXiv:2611.03078v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-source remote sensing image classification benefits from complementary spectral and structural information. However, identifying discriminative cross-modal features remains challenging. This letter proposes a Cross-Layer Refinement and Frequency-aware Fusion Network (CRFNet) within a lightweight dual-branch architecture. Specifically, a Cross-Layer Refinement Attention (CLRA) module propagates selected attention relationships across successive layers and employs top relation selection to progressively strengthen discriminative spatial dependencies while suppressing irrelevant responses. Furthermore, a Frequency-aware Complementary Fusion (FCF) module combines frequency-wise interactions with cross-modal channel attention in the Fourier domain. The resulting representations are then converted into spatial-domain gates to selectively modulate complementary features. Experiments on the Houston 2013 and Augsburg datasets demonstrate that the proposed CRFNet consistently outperforms several state-of-the-art methods. The codes are publicly available at https://github.com/oucailab/CRFNet
item.dc:creator: Wenhan Xiao, Chuanzheng Gong, Feng Gao, Junyu Dong, Qian Du

item.title: View optimization in Computed Tomography
item.description: arXiv:2611.03322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many emerging CT imaging applications must operate with data from sparse projection angles, on the order of 10 views, such as first responder scenarios, dynamic imaging of detonation events, and flash imaging of materials under extreme conditions in high energy-density science. Few-view imaging is a data undersampling problem, that degrades tomographic reconstructions with streaks, shadows, and other aliasing artifacts, due to ill-conditioning. In few- view CT, the specific set of projection angles can strongly impact reconstruction quality, and the optimal angles depend on the object being scanned. Despite a surge of recent research, there is much to explore in this problem. We present an object-aware performance prediction framework for few-view projection datasets based on a matrix decomposition of the discretized forward model augmented with expected object gradient information. The method yields a quantitative score for a candidate set of view angles that can underpin a view selection recommendation algorithm. A key feature is that it can be applied at multiple stages of acquisition: a priori, before any radiographs are taken, or adaptively, after some radiographs are collected, to determine the next best view. We demonstrate the approach using simulated CT data with 5 view and 15 view configurations. Preliminary results are encouraging; images reconstructed using a standard statistical algorithm show that reconstruction accuracy agrees with our performance score. Reconstruction accuracy was evaluated against a known ground truth using an information theoretic score. Continued testing with complex objects and multiple geometries is necessary.
item.dc:creator: Seemeen Karimi, Christopher McGuire

item.title: Air-Scan-Based Point-Spread-Function Estimation for Megavoltage CT with Flat-Panel Detectors
item.description: arXiv:2611.03359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate spatial-resolution characterization of flat-panel detectors at megavoltage energies is difficult due to long-tailed cross-talk. Conventional measurements at high energy using line-pair gauges or knife-edge phantoms require expensive, carefully fabricated objects and precise alignment, and despite these, scatter from the phantom, detector, and imaging room can further confound the measurement. We present a method for estimating the detector point spread function (PSF) from the mean noise power spectrum (NPS) calculated from repeated radiographs in air. The approach is mathematically equivalent to an autocovariance-based method but is more practical for long-tailed PSFs. We validate the method using simulated air data and Monte Carlo N-particle (MCNP6) calculations of energy deposition in a flat-panel detector. We show that deconvolving the experimental PSF increases the accuracy of transmission radiographs of step wedges. The method requires no phantom or alignments and is straightforward to reproduce.
item.dc:creator: Seemeen Karimi, Joseph Bendahan, K. Aditya Mohan

item.title: Extended Field-of-View Passive mmWave Imaging Using Implicit Neural Representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.03396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a self-supervised learning-based framework for expanding the field-of-view (FoV) of passive real-aperture millimeter wave (mmWave) imaging systems. Our framework exploits aliasing artifacts/grating lobes---which are an inherent part of mmWave image formation---to expand FoV. Specifically, we recognize that removing aliasing artifacts can be cast as an underdetermined deconvolution problem and that in solving this problem, one can expand the system's FoV. We solve this deconvolution problem and expand the system's FoV by enforcing temporal regularity with time-varying Implicit Neural Representations (INRs). We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through extensive simulations and real-world experiments with Phase Sensitive Innovation's (PSI) state-of-the-art electro-optical modulation based passive mmWave imaging system.
item.dc:creator: Sanjaya Herath, Matthew R. Ziemann, Christopher A. Metzler

item.title: Scaling global tractography with ExaTract: from large cohorts to ultra-high-resolution datasets
item.description: arXiv:2611.03419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Global tractography offers a theoretical framework for reconstructing white matter connectivity from diffusion MRI by jointly inferring all streamlines and their consistency with the diffusion signal and underlying anatomical priors. However, its sequential nature and log-linear complexity make it computationally prohibitive at the scales demanded by neuroimaging, from large population cohorts such as the Human Connectome Project (HCP) to ex vivo ultra-high-field acquisitions at mesoscopic resolution. In this work, we present ExaTract, a parallelized spin-glass tractography framework designed for high-performance computing (HPC) architectures. Implemented as an open-source MPI+Kokkos application, ExaTract partitions the tractography domain into spatially overlapping regions processed across distributed memory nodes, with regular synchronization of boundary modifications to preserve global convergence guarantees. We validate ExaTract on both in vivo and ex vivo diffusion MRI data: the complete HCP dataset demonstrates population-scale throughput, while the high-resolution Chenonceau dataset provides the first mesoscopic structural connectome derived from global tractography.
item.dc:creator: Simon Legeay, Felix Matuschke, Bastien Herlin, Jan Andr\'e Reuter, Christophe Destrieux, Markus Axer, Ivy Uszynski, Cyril Poupon

item.title: HIVE-Diff: High Frame Rate HDR Video Reconstruction from a Single LDR Frame and Events
item.description: arXiv:2611.03465v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High frame rate HDR video is important in applications such as autonomous driving and scientific imaging, where rapid motion and extreme illumination often occur simultaneously. Conventional frame cameras face a trade-off between temporal resolution and dynamic range, while event cameras provide complementary high-speed brightness-change measurements over a wide illumination range. These properties have motivated event-based HDR reconstruction, with existing methods broadly following event-only and hybrid event-frame paradigms. Event-only HDR reconstruction, however, suffers from brightness and color drift due to the lack of absolute intensity references. Hybrid event-frame methods alleviate this ambiguity using low-dynamic-range (LDR) frames as anchors, but most perform one-to-one HDR reconstruction at available LDR timestamps. In this work, we investigate single-reference HDR temporal expansion, reconstructing N HDR frames from one LDR reference and events instead of N aligned LDR observations. We develop HIVE-Diff, an event-conditioned video diffusion framework that decomposes the task into event-guided temporal generation and HDR content completion. Because paired real HDR-event data are scarce, we train on synthetic data and adapt the model to real event domains using LDR-event sequences as proxy supervision with teacher-student distillation. Experiments on synthetic and multiple real-world datasets demonstrate strong reconstruction quality and robust real-data adaptation.
item.dc:creator: Caixin Wang, Qingrui Wang, Jie Zhang, Ralph Etienne-Cummings

item.title: Toward Artifact-Free Dermoscopy: Characterization of ISIC 2019 Image Defects for Deep Learning Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.03502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The International Skin Imaging Collaboration (ISIC) archive offers the largest publicly available collection of dermoscopic images for skin lesion analysis. However, the ISIC 2019 dataset suffers from several acquisition artifacts such as hair occlusions, vignetting, surgical ink markings, and ruler scales, all of which compromise its utility in deep learning workflows by introducing non-biological visual structures. To address these limitations, we present a rigorously annotated version of ISIC 2019 that includes binary masks for key artifact types. Ink marks and vignetting were annotated through systematic manual review and iterative refinement using professional image editing software. For hair and ruler artifacts, we implemented a semi-automatic pipeline based on our previously developed deep learning architecture, ChimeraNet. Automated predictions were then manually corrected as needed for precision. The resulting dataset supports both the development of our own melanoma detection model and broader community research requiring artifact-mitigated dermoscopic images.
item.dc:creator: Victoria Wegley, Joshua Hoog, Tristan Crawford, Keith Miller, William Fons, Kacy Pugh, Jackson Taylor, Sami Swinfard, Avigail Fernandes, Gehana Patel, Jason Hagerty, William V. Stoecker, R. Joe Stanley

item.title: SFA: A Statistical Physics-Inspired Diffusion Transformer for Efficient and High-Quality Image Generation
item.description: arXiv:2611.00027v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Diffusion transformers have achieved remarkable success in image generation, but accelerating attention while preserving generation quality remains a major challenge at high resolutions. Inspired by statistical physics and the widespread occurrence of scale-free laws in nature, we introduce Scale-Free Attention (SFA), which preserves fine local interactions while summarizing distant regions at progressively coarser scales. For $N$ tokens, mean pooling, token-count correction, and a shared softmax over a scale-free spatial hierarchy give SFA $O(N\log N)$ complexity in both forward and backward passes. Our Triton implementation achieves $357.3\times$ forward and $265.6\times$ backward attention speedups over FlashAttention at 262,144 tokens. After 40 epochs of PixelFlow training from scratch on ImageNet at $256\times256$ resolution, SFA achieves the best generation quality among five attention mechanisms, including full attention. Fr\'echet inception distance evaluated on 50,000 generated samples (FID-50k) improves from 13.25 for full attention to 12.51, and the advantage over full attention persists through 80 epochs. SFA also achieves the best generation quality among the compared efficient-attention methods on Flickr-Faces-HQ (FFHQ). Beyond training from scratch, Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium with attention replaced by SFA retains the generation quality of its full-attention counterpart under matched fine-tuning budgets. We obtain similar results when fine-tuning pretrained PixelFlow on ImageNet. SFA establishes scale-free structure as an effective design principle for efficient, high-quality diffusion transformers.
item.dc:creator: Zixuan Huang (School of Computer Science, Peking University, Beijing, China, School of Physics, Peking University, Beijing, China), Tianhao You (School of Computer Science, Peking University, Beijing, China), Guozhang Chen (School of Computer Science, Peking University, Beijing, China, National Engineering Research Center of Visual Technology, Peking University, Beijing, China)

item.title: Out-of-distribution AI-generated image detection with zero-phase deconvolution for residual whitening
item.description: arXiv:2611.00043v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Current AI-generated image detection methods struggle in out-of-distribution testing conditions because detectors are usually not robust when evaluated on generators not included in the training set. This work explores a way to mitigate the forensic bias between sources of images -whether real or generated -by removing generator-specific fingerprints. This new training process can be approximated by pre-processing involving a deconvolution operation designed to remove correlated noise patterns inducing loss of generalization. Indeed, we show that whitening the spatial distribution of the image noise residuals can significantly improve the performance of detectors on images coming from generators unseen during training. In particular, an end-to-end CNN model trained on whitened image residuals improves detection by 12.6% on average compared to a training involving original images.
item.dc:creator: Yusuf Yigit Pilavc{\i} (UNICAEN, GREYC), Antoine Mallet (CRIStAL), Vincent Itier (IMT Nord Europe, CRIStAL, CERI SN - IMT Nord Europe), Jan Butora (CRIStAL), J\'er\'emie Boulanger (CRIStAL), Patrick Bas (CRIStAL)

item.title: Detector-Integrated Multi-Cue Association for Occlusion-Aware UAV Multi-Object Tracking
item.description: arXiv:2611.00105v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-object tracking (MOT) in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery is challenging because vehicles are small, visually similar, and frequently occluded, which leads to identity switches (IDSW). Appearance-based trackers such as DeepSORT rely on a standalone re-identification (ReID) network, whose per-target inference limits runtime speed, while the appearance of small or occluded vehicles remains unreliable. This paper proposes a detector-integrated multi-cue tracking framework. Lightweight projection heads are attached to the neck of the YOLOv8n detector to extract target embeddings through ROIAlign, producing detections and embeddings in a single forward pass. A multi-cue association cost then combines motion, IoU, and appearance distances with weights determined through ablation, complemented by low-score rescue and appearance-memory protection. On the UAVDT benchmark, the proposed method achieves a MOTA of 28.33, a HOTA of 31.16, and an IDF1 of 38.18 at 82.59 FPS, the best among the compared trackers in all three metrics, and reduces IDSW by 58.4\% compared with DeepSORT.
item.dc:creator: Shu-Hung Chou, Trong-An Bui, Wei-Ming Chen, Hsin-Piao Lin

item.title: Synergy-Aware Symbol Allocation for Distributed Semantic Communication
item.description: arXiv:2611.00648v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Distributed semantic communication enables spatially separated terminals to support collaborative inference over wireless links for 6G edge intelligence. In multimodal sensing and cooperative perception, a single terminal captures only a partial view, and full task semantics emerge only when complementary observations from multiple terminals are fused at the receiver. However, under tight uplink budgets, existing task-oriented joint source--channel coding (JSCC) and distributed information bottleneck (IB) methods evaluate rate--distortion trade-offs per terminal, tending to undervalue cross-terminal synergistic features and prune them prematurely. To address this issue, we propose a synergy-credited distributed JSCC (\method{}) framework that introduces a differentiable, post-equalization matrix R\'enyi synergy credit as a surrogate to reward complementary task evidence surviving the wireless channel and backpropagates its gradients to local symbol gates. At deployment, the credit branch is removed and binary symbol masks are frozen, allowing each terminal to encode independently without inter-terminal signaling or extra inference overhead. Experiments show that \method{} recovers the analytical symbol-selection threshold on parity sources and reduces payload symbols by 28.4\% on AV-MNIST and 32.9\% on PAMAP2 over an uncredited gated baseline, while achieving a 6.2-point accuracy gain at $-6$~dB under 3GPP TDL-C fading with pilot-aided channel estimation for low-overhead wireless cooperative sensing.
item.dc:creator: Fan Gao, Youzheng Wang, Zhijin Qin, Xiaoming Tao

item.title: Event-Based Optical Flow Constraint via Time-Sliced Plane Fitting
item.description: arXiv:2611.01960v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Event-based optical flow estimation using spatiotemporal planar approximation inherently assumes constant velocity and tends to average out temporal velocity variations. In this paper, we propose a flow estimation method that extends this planar approximation along the temporal axis. The resulting event-based optical flow constraint allows existing variational optical flow formulations to model temporal motion variation. Specifically, we partition the space-time volume into sub-intervals and apply a two-step planar approximation to track object edges consistently. Moreover, a spatial compensation mechanism and a temporal regularization term are incorporated to compensate for edge displacements and temporally stabilize the flow estimation, respectively. The experimental results show that modeling temporal motion variation improves flow estimation accuracy over conventional methods.
item.dc:creator: Masaki Koike, Yusuke Kameda, Shunichi Sato, Takayuki Hamamoto

item.title: DINOFAS: Bonafide-Centric Representation Learning for Face Anti-Spoofing
item.description: arXiv:2611.02756v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Face anti-spoofing (FAS) models often learn attack- and dataset-specific cues that degrade performance under unseen acquisition conditions and presentation attacks. We present DINOFAS, a DINOv3-based framework that formulates FAS as bonafide-centric representation learning. The proposed framework combines parameter-efficient DINOv3 adaptation using low-rank adaptation (LoRA), an attention style-content disentanglement (ASCD) module for reducing domain-specific appearance variations, and a dual-branch architecture that separates prototype-based liveness learning from attack-semantic supervision. The model is jointly optimized using a bonafide-centric prototype objective, an attack-semantic classification loss applied to detached features, and orthogonality regularization. DINOFAS achieves an average HTER of 9.09\% under the standard OCIM leave-one-domain-out protocol, where training is performed on three source datasets and evaluation is conducted on the held-out unseen domain. We further evaluate synthetic-to-real generalization by training exclusively on SynthASpoof and testing on four unseen real-world datasets, where DINOFAS achieves the lowest average HTER of 21.41\% and the highest average AUC of 86.14\% among the compared methods. Evaluations on OULU-NPU and SiW-Mv2 additionally demonstrate robustness to variations in acquisition conditions, devices, and unseen presentation attacks.
item.dc:creator: Shakeel Muhammad Ibrahim, Muhammad Sohail Ibrahim, Muhammad Shahid Jabbar, Shujaat Khan

item.title: Progressive Multi-Scale Super-Resolution via Cascaded Bicubic Anchors and Inter-Scale Mutual Refinement
item.description: arXiv:2611.03390v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Super-resolution networks are trained for one magnification factor, so several output resolutions require several models. We propose PMS-SR, a progressive single-input multiple-output network that produces x2, x4, and x8 results in one forward pass, with a Transformer backbone on the low-resolution grid. In Stage 1, each scale is predicted as a residual over the detached bicubic upsampling of the previous scale's prediction. With Dirac and zero initialization, training starts exactly from the bicubic cascade, and each head adds only the band the previous scale lacks. In Stage 2, inter-scale mutual refinement couples the scales in both directions through space-to-depth feedback, deformable alignment, and per-pixel fusion, so x8 features refine the x2 output. Trained on DF2K, the 7.95M-parameter model achieves a higher PSNR than every compared multi-scale method at x4 and x8 on all five standard benchmarks. At x8, it outperforms the x8-specific DRN-L on all of them, leads all compared methods on Urban100, and is within 0.13 dB of the best result elsewhere. Against three single-scale SwinIR-M models, PMS-SR uses 22% of the parameters, runs 2.9x faster on BSD100 inputs, and its outputs agree 6.7-12.4 dB more closely. Code and pretrained models will be released at https://github.com/julian135707/PMS-SR upon acceptance.
item.dc:creator: Chun-An Lin, Yu-Chia Chang, Chi-Mao Fan, Yen-Chieh Ouyang, Tsung-Jung Liu

item.title: Learning-based Axial Video Motion Magnification
item.description: arXiv:2312.09551v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Video motion magnification amplifies invisible small motions to be perceptible, which provides humans with a spatially dense and holistic understanding of small motions in the scene of interest. This is based on the premise that magnifying small motions enhances the legibility of motions. In the real world, however, vibrating objects often possess convoluted systems that have complex natural frequencies, modes, and directions. Existing motion magnification often fails to improve legibility since the intricate motions still retain complex characteristics even after being magnified, which may distract us from analyzing them. In this work, we focus on improving legibility by proposing a new concept, axial motion magnification, which magnifies decomposed motions along the user-specified direction. Axial motion magnification can be applied to various applications where motions of specific axes are critical, by providing simplified and easily readable motion information. To achieve this, we propose a novel Motion Separation Module that enables to disentangle and magnify the motion representation along axes of interest. Furthermore, we build a new synthetic training dataset for the axial motion magnification task. Our proposed method improves the legibility of resulting motions along certain axes by adding a new feature: user controllability. Axial motion magnification is a more generalized concept; thus, our method can be directly adapted to the generic motion magnification and achieves favorable performance against competing methods.
item.dc:creator: Kwon Byung-Ki, Oh Hyun-Bin, Kim Jun-Seong, Hyunwoo Ha, Tae-Hyun Oh

item.title: A Novel Approach to Chest X-ray Lung Segmentation Using U-net and Modified Convolutional Block Attention Module
item.description: arXiv:2404.14322v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Lung segmentation in chest X-ray (CXR) images is a crucial task in medical image analysis, aiding in accurate disease diagnosis and treatment planning. This study presents an improved U-Net architecture by integrating a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to enhance segmentation performance. The proposed CBAM unifies three attention mechanisms (Channel Attention, Spatial Attention, and Pixel Attention) to refine feature extraction and improve focus on critical image regions. The Channel Attention mechanism emphasizes inter-channel dependencies, the Spatial Attention mechanism enhances localization accuracy by highlighting spatial correlations, and the Pixel Attention mechanism refines segmentation precision at the pixel level. By incorporating CBAM into the U-Net framework, the model achieves superior performance in lung segmentation, as evaluated using the Dice coefficient and Jaccard similarity index. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly improves segmentation accuracy, making it a promising advancement in medical image processing for lung disease assessment.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Ali Labbaf Khaniki, Marzieh Mirzaeibonehkhater, Mohammad Manthouri, Katayoon Faraji

item.title: Programmable Silicon Retina on Pixel Processor Array
item.description: arXiv:2606.08370v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Standard dynamic vision sensors approximate retinal processing by detecting temporal contrast changes, offering high speed and high dynamic range. In this work, we explore whether incorporating additional biologically inspired processing stages - specifically spatial filtering and gain control - can offer advantages for certain downstream tasks such as saliency prediction. We present the first implementation of a multi-stage Silicon Retina model on the SCAMP-5 Pixel Processor Array, along with a GPU-based simulation framework. We evaluate the performance of our model on Video Intensity Reconstruction and Video Saliency Prediction. While the bio-inspired model is less effective at reconstructing absolute intensity frames, it achieves a 13\% reduction in saliency prediction loss in comparison to standard DVS event representation, while reducing the event rate by approximately 47\%. These experiments are obtained using a lightweight $\approx 100$k-parameter FireNet-style network, adapted from event-based reconstruction to saliency prediction. These results suggest that the silicon retina's "information distillation" mechanism can achieve a more efficient representation for downstream neural networks, particularly in bandwidth-constrained edge applications.
item.dc:creator: Maciej Lewandowski, Prince Philip, Alexandre Marcireau, Chetan Singh Thakur, Andr\'e van Schaik, Piotr Dudek

item.title: Multimodal Deep Learning for Uncertainty-Aware Radiation Pneumonitis Risk Prediction
item.description: arXiv:2608.28937v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Radiation pneumonitis (RP) is a potentially serious complication of thoracic radiotherapy, making reliable risk prediction important for identifying high-risk patients and guiding effective toxicity management. Although deep learning models can predict RP risk, uncertainty quantification remains underdeveloped in radiation toxicity assessment. We developed a Multimodal Bayesian Diffusion Transformer (MM-DiT) that integrates pretreatment computed tomography (CT) and three-dimensional planning dose distributions for RP risk prediction and uncertainty quantification. MM-DiT combines self-supervised multimodal representation learning with Bayesian classification to estimate individual risk and characterize aleatoric, epistemic, and label uncertainty. In independent Mount Sinai Health System (MSHS) and RTOG cohorts, MM-DiT achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of $0.89$ and $0.86$, respectively, with expected calibration errors of $0.02$ and $0.03$. Incorporating post-treatment CT increased AUC to $0.95$ in MSHS and reduced aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty by approximately $40-45\%$ and $40\%$, respectively. These findings establish a framework for uncertainty-aware radiation toxicity prediction that complements risk estimates with information about predictive reliability. By integrating multimodal learning and uncertainty quantification, MM-DiT may advance more interpretable and trustworthy AI-assisted toxicity assessment and support individualized radiotherapy planning.
item.dc:creator: Jin Yang, Tian Liu, Jing Wang, Sooyun Caroline Tavolacci, Benjamin Tran, Rajwanth Veluswamy, Kenneth E. Rosenzweig, Julie Bloom, Robert M. Samstein, Ming Chao

item.title: Resolution-Flexible Decoding for Hybrid Neural Video Representations
item.description: arXiv:2609.23555v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Neural video representations (NVRs) represent videos using neural network parameters and, in hybrid formulations, frame-wise latent embeddings. In conventional hybrid NVRs, the spatial size of frame-wise latent embeddings and the decoder upsampling schedule depend on the target resolution, potentially requiring large and non-uniform upsampling factors. In this paper, we propose a resolution-flexible decoder framework for hybrid NVRs. The decoder is constructed from uniform \(2\times\) upsampling stages, whose target feature sizes are obtained by tracing the spatial resolution backward from the final output resolution. After each upsampling stage, the feature map is aligned with the target size by minimal padding or cropping when necessary. To support this progressive decoding process, we further use intermediate reconstruction supervision and a reconstruction-difficulty-aware frame sampling strategy based on recent frame-wise losses. The framework preserves the basic representation format of hybrid NVRs and can therefore be applied to different backbones. Experiments on the UVG dataset at resolutions of \(1080\times1920\) and \(810\times1440\) show that the proposed approach improves reconstruction quality over the corresponding NVR baselines.
item.dc:creator: Taiga Hayami, Masaya Takabe, Hiroshi Watanabe

item.title: Hybrid++: The Bridge between PDE Models and Deep Learning for Gamma Noise Removal
item.description: arXiv:2610.08892v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multiplicative gamma noise is one of the dominant noise factors in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and medical ultrasound images. They are dependent on pixel level noises due to which they are highly varying across the image and harder to handle as compared to additive noise. The denoising methods to address this noise currently include classical partial differential equation (PDE) methods which are good for interpretation but lack the restoration ability as compared to the state-of-the-art models while deep neural networks like DnCNN achieve high performance but at the cost of transparency due to which practitioners are skeptical to use them in high-risk critical fields like medicine. This paper presents Hybrid++, a novel trainable nonlinear reaction-diffusion architecture that addresses both the concerns - staying interpretable while offering performance close to huge black-box models. It combines a fully learnable PDE initialization with a 3-stage reaction-diffusion network having 64-channel multiscale filter banks, 4-layer Squeeze-and-Excitation attention-based influence functions and a 64-dimensional noise level embedding. It uses a two-phase training strategy, stage-wise optimization followed by joint end-to-end refinement which enables co-adaptation of all learnable parameters. On the FoE benchmark, Hybrid++ substantially improves over classical PDE, BM3D and the original TNRD baselines. In the severe-noise setting L=1, it comes within 0.23 dB PSNR of a separately trained DnCNN while using only about 8% of its parameters.
item.dc:creator: Mahipal Jetta, Sujato Dutta

item.title: Per-Bundle, Pre-Reconstruction Inversion for Temporal CT: Flux-Compensation Design and Training-Free Empirical-Bayes Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2610.19229v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In Temporal computed tomography (TCT) each detector reading sums the photons of up to three rays. Earlier work set the resulting per-bundle limits and tested a learned prior on one patient at one incident count $N_0$; this paper lifts both. N$_0$FC ($N_0$ flux compensation), a bow-tie and tube-current-modulation co-design, equalizes each bundle's detected flux. SNN2 is a per-bundle Poisson maximum-likelihood estimator. V8c is a neural-network corrector trained on 19 patients stratified by water-equivalent diameter (WED). T2bp, a training-free empirical-Bayes post-processor, combines per-bundle Poisson likelihoods with a prior built from the patient's own bundles. Results use that work's Dose Inflation Factor (DIF), charging bias as error. On 23 non-test volumes, N$_0$FC lowers the per-volume median middle-path Cramer-Rao floor, as a DIF, from 23-48 under a flat-fluence (no bow-tie) baseline to 3.3-6.3 at 35-62% of its incident photons, near the equal-attenuation value 13/3 and 1.4-1.7 times below conventional bow-ties; the bow-tie alone achieves this median, and tube-current modulation trims the tail. For bundles with $X_2<6$ (83%), SNN2 attains this floor (median mean-squared-error ratio 1.02); training-free T2bp$\circ$SNN2 lowers the ratio to 0.89 (0.74-1.26). It is best or tied on three of four N$_0$FC test cells (WED 207-342 mm) and trails T2bp$\circ$V8c by 3% on the fourth. V8c beats SNN2 in distribution under baseline acquisition, gains at most 9% under N$_0$FC (losing 14% on the largest in-distribution test patient), and fails on a patient acquired below its training count level. Acquisition co-design removes most of the attenuation-contrast penalty, and training-free estimation attains the resulting limit. The remaining three- to six-fold gap to single-source CT at equal fluence, and the high-attenuation tail, are targets for inter-bundle priors.
item.dc:creator: Guy M Besson

item.title: Stochastic Generative Plug-and-Play Priors
item.description: arXiv:2604.03603v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Plug-and-play (PnP) methods are widely used for solving imaging inverse problems by incorporating a denoiser into an optimization algorithm. Score-based diffusion models (SBDMs) have recently demonstrated strong generative performance via a denoiser trained across a wide range of noise levels. Despite their shared reliance on denoisers, it remains unclear how to systematically use SBDMs as priors within the PnP framework without relying on reverse diffusion sampling. In this paper, we establish a score-based interpretation of PnP that justifies using pretrained SBDMs directly within PnP algorithms. Building on this connection, we introduce a stochastic generative PnP (SGPnP) framework that uses stochastic re-noising to better leverage the broad noise-level conditioning of pretrained SBDMs, significantly improving reconstruction quality in severely ill-posed inverse problems. We show that noise injection induces optimization on a Gaussian-smoothed objective and enables avoidance of strict saddle points under suitable conditions. Experiments on challenging inverse tasks, such as multi-coil MRI reconstruction and large-mask natural image inpainting, demonstrate consistent improvement over conventional PnP methods and achieve performance competitive with diffusion-based solvers.
item.dc:creator: Chicago Y. Park, Edward P. Chandler, Yuyang Hu, Michael T. McCann, Cristina Garcia-Cardona, Brendt Wohlberg, Ulugbek S. Kamilov

item.title: Efficient Factorized Volume Synthesis with Lifted Inter-Slice Feature Trajectories
item.description: arXiv:2605.19060v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: High-resolution 3D medical image generation remains challenging because fully volumetric models are computationally expensive, while efficient 2D slice generators often fail to preserve anatomical consistency across the third dimension. We propose LiFT, a framework for Lifted inter-slice Feature Trajectories that factorizes 3D volume synthesis into per-slice image generation and inter-slice trajectory learning. Rather than using a fully volumetric synthesis backbone, LiFT treats a volume as an ordered trajectory in feature space, capturing how anatomical structures appear, transform, and disappear across depth. We demonstrate the LiFT framework in both unconditional and conditional settings. In unconditional generation, a tri-planar drifting loss matches feature distributions between generated and real volumes across three orthogonal planes; in paired translation, a bidirectional $z$-context mixer trained with paired target supervision supplies through-plane coherence while preserving per-slice fidelity. We evaluate LiFT on BraTS 2023 for unconditional and missing-modality MR synthesis, and on SynthRAD2023 for MR-to-CT translation. LiFT achieves competitive image quality while retaining the efficiency of predominantly 2D synthesis, operating up to $390\times$ faster than a volumetric diffusion baseline and consistently improving through-plane coherence through explicit inter-slice modeling. These results establish lightweight inter-slice trajectory learning as an efficient approach to high-resolution 3D medical synthesis.
item.dc:creator: Xinhe Zhang, Yuyang Zhang, Pengfei Jin, Arnau Marin-Llobet, Na Li, Quanzheng Li

item.title: Non-frontal face recognition using GANs and memristor-based classifiers
item.description: arXiv:2606.12074v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Face recognition systems have advanced significantly through deep learning techniques, delivering high performance and robustness in complex scenarios. However, these approaches incur substantial computational overhead, limiting their in situ applicability in resource-constrained platforms such as drones, where they can address challenges including non-frontal facial imagery. Memristor-based neuromorphic systems have emerged as a compelling approach for edge AI applications, combining biologically inspired processing with efficient and scalable computation. In this work, we propose a facial recognition framework that addresses non-frontal pose variations by integrating lightweight generative adversarial network (GAN)-based pose frontalisation with memristor-based neuromorphic recognition. The experimental results on two datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of combining adversarial learning with memristive technology, achieving up to 96% identification accuracy. The proposed approach alleviates the computational bottlenecks of conventional AI and offers a scalable, efficient solution for face recognition in dynamic real-world environments.
item.dc:creator: Semih Vazgecen, Cristian Sestito, Spyros Stathopoulos, Themis Prodromakis

item.title: Entity-Aware Evaluation of OCR Systems for Historical Document Transcription
item.description: arXiv:2610.33004v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is essential for digitizing historical archives, yet standard evaluation metrics such as Character Error Rate (CER) do not necessarily reflect whether meaningful information, such as names, dates, and identifiers, is preserved. In this work, we investigate entitylevel analysis of OCR errors as a complementary perspective for evaluating OCR quality in historical documents. Using a publicly available benchmark of 175 documents from the Berrutti Archive, augmented with 5,209 manually annotated entity mentions that will be released upon acceptance, we compare sequence-recognition OCR systems, OCR-specialized vision-language models, and general-purpose vision-language models. Beyond global transcription accuracy, we analyze entity preservation and recoverability under varying character-level edit tolerances. Our experiments show that OCR rankings depend on the evaluation criterion: while Qwen 3.6 achieves the highest entity coverage across all tested tolerances, several systems with lower exact-match coverage recover substantially when small errors are tolerated, suggesting that many of their errors correspond to localized character-level deviations rather than fundamentally incorrect entity transcriptions. Conversely, some systems remain unable to recover many entities even under relaxed matching. These findings show that OCR quality cannot be fully characterized by aggregate transcription metrics alone and highlight the importance of evaluating how OCR errors affect the preservation and recoverability of meaningful information.
